title: Integrator pair-program runbook + 10min demo script
content:
Purpose
---
This is a compact runbook for pairing with integrator engineering teams during their first integration with Redwood SDKs. The goal: a low-friction 10-minute demo + 30–60 minute pairing session that gets them to a reproducible sample app, with telemetry and basic failure handling wired. Keep it opinionated, small, and repeatable.

When to use
- Early-stage integration calls (first technical sync)
- Workshop slot during onboarding week
- Tech-screen with partner engineers who want hands-on help

Core outcomes (measurable)
- Partner runs a sample request end-to-end from their machine (local or sandbox)
- Minimal telemetry (request id, latency, error type) appears in our sample dashboard
- They can reproduce a common failure and apply the suggested mitigation

Preflight checklist (5–10 min before pairing)
- Confirm partner has: API key (sandbox), Node or Python environment, git, and a terminal
- Share pre-cloned repo link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/tree/mini-onramp
- Turn on screen sharing + request they open terminal + IDE (or use Live Share)
- Load this mini checklist in Slack for the meeting notes

Materials to open during session
- README quickstart in repo (open in editor)
- sample telemetry dashboard (Grafana link — ask SRE for sandbox view)
- this runbook (for timing and failure scripts)

10-minute demo script (run time + script bullets)
0:00–0:60s — 1 min: kickoff and expectations - One-line intro: "Today we’ll get a sample request running from your laptop and see basic telemetry—after that we’ll pair on extending your use case." - Confirm language (Python/Node) - Confirm they want local mode or sandbox API
1:00–3:00 — 2 min: run prewritten sample (happy path)
- Command: pip install -r requirements.txt && export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-sandbox-... && python quickstart.py
- Talking points: show the single API call, highlight model param and stream vs non-stream option
- Expected output: generated text + request id printed to console
3:00–5:00 — 2 min: inspect telemetry (live)
- Open sample dashboard and filter by request id printed earlier
- Show latency, token count, and HTTP status
- Point out: where error traces would show up (if applicable)
5:00–7:00 — 2 min: simulate a network failure and retry pattern
- In a second terminal: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/break (this is a local test harness in the repo)
- Run the sample again and observe graceful fallback log message: "retrying on transient 5xx"
- Show how SDK backoff is configurable in config.yml
7:00–9:00 — 2 min: demonstrate an optimization knob (batching or cache)
- Toggle BATCHING=false in the sample env and rerun a small loop script that sends 10 requests
- Show difference in per-request latency and token-per-request cost (sample printed metrics)
9:00–10:00 — 1 min: wrap and next steps
- Summarize what was achieved and propose pairing topics for the deep session: authentication, private deployment concerns, and quality monitoring

Pairing session guide (30–60 minutes)
- Start by collecting their real use case and acceptance criteria
- Scaffold: copy the quickstart file to src/integrator-demo and change prompt to a short real example
- Add basic telemetry tags: team=payments, env=staging, feature=smart-summaries
- Introduce two quick experiments: 1) change model size for cost vs quality 2) enable prefix caching and run a 5-request conversational loop

Common pain points + troubleshooting snippets
- Issue: "API key unauthorized" Fix: check REDWOOD_API_KEY env var; show example: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...; curl https://api.redwood.com/v1/ping -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY"
- Issue: "requests slow / timeouts" Fix: check batching config, confirm region selection, run small perf test: python perf_ping.py --qps 5 --seq 64
- Issue: "no telemetry appears" Fix: confirm SDK instrumentation enabled (ENV REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=1), confirm request_id present, check sample dashboard filter by request_id

Telemetry: what to capture by default (opinionated minimal set)
- request_id (uuids)
- sdk_version
- model_id / model_variant
- latency_ms
- tokens_in / tokens_out
- http_status / error_type
- env / team / feature_tag

Sample log line (single-line JSON)
{"timestamp":"2025-01-09T10:12:05Z","request_id":"b2f9-...","model_id":"redwood-1.3","latency_ms":132,"tokens_in":45,"tokens_out":120,"status":200}

Quick telemetry queries (for the partner to paste)
- Avg latency past 1h: SELECT avg(latency_ms) FROM requests WHERE team='payments' AND time > now() - 1h
- Errors by type: SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE status >= 500 GROUP BY error_type

Mini code snippets (safe, copy-paste friendly)
Python quickstart (quickstart.py)
```
import os
from redwood import RedwoodClient

client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
resp = client.generate(model='redwood-1.3', prompt='Summarize this: ...')
print(resp.text)
print('request id:', resp.request_id)
```
Node quickstart (index.mjs)
```
import Redwood from 'redwood'
const client = new Redwood(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY)
const r = await client.generate({model:'redwood-1.3', prompt:'Summarize this'})
console.log(r.text, 'id=', r.requestId)
```
(These are intentionally minimal—point partners to the repo for expanded examples including streaming and function-calls.)

Safety and data handling notes (verbal bullets)
- By default sandbox keys do not persist customer data to long-term storage
- For production, discuss Private deployment or Dedicated capacity if they need isolation
- Remind: PII should be redacted before sending to any hosted endpoint unless customer has a compliance exception

Follow-up deliverables (send within 24h)
- A forked repo branch with their modified sample app: feature/integrator-<company>-quickstart
- A short recording (5–15 min) of the runthrough and telemetry filter steps
- A small ticket with proposed SLA/region/throughput needs (JIRA template below)

JIRA ticket template (copy into issue body)
- Summary: "Onboard <company> - initial integration and throughput request"
- Acceptance criteria:
  - sample app runs locally with sandbox key
  - telemetry visible in shared dashboard
  - initial throughput target: 50 rps / 1k tokens avg per req

Notes to facilitator (voice-of-experienced-engineer)
- Keep the first 10 minutes focused on the visible win (print request id + open dashboard)
- Don’t try to solve private deployment questions in the first call—capture them as follow-ups
- Encourage pair-programming: ask partner to type and run commands; tell them you’ll take keyboard only if they ask

Open questions / experiment ideas
- Could we ship a one-click Live Share link that preloads the repo, env, and dashboard filter? (Product ask)
- Can we auto-generate a short recording from the sandbox environment when a sample runs?

Appendix: useful commands
- clone & start: git clone ... && cd sdk-examples/mini-onramp && ./start-local.sh
- perf quick: python perf_ping.py --qps 5 --seq 32
- simulate 5xx: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/break

End of runbook.
